findings.passage: First was Tuesday with House Concurrent Resolution 5004 , which amends the state constitution to add citizenship as a requirement for voting in any election.
findings.note: Newsletter in his name describes the House debate and vote on HCR 5004 (citizenship as a voting requirement in the state constitution). The same column closes with 'I voted yes on each bill, and each passed their floor votes.'

findings.passage: The second was on Wednesday with House Bill (HB) 2020 , which requires a quarterly report from the director of division of vehicles listing the names and addresses of noncitizens that have attained driver’s licenses in said period.
findings.note: Newsletter in his name describes HB 2020, a quarterly list of noncitizens holding driver's licenses, debated and voted that week; he states he voted yes on each bill.

findings.passage: HB 2016 , this bill adds published online obituaries as sufficient criteria for election officers to remove deceased voters from voter rolls, under state law.
findings.note: Newsletter in his name lists HB 2016 (deceased voters removed from rolls using online obituaries) among bills debated and passed by the House.

findings.passage: This bill would restrict online voter registration to only government run websites, with a .gov domain, or websites vetted and chosen by the Secretary of State, upon meeting several security criteria, like data encryption.
findings.note: Newsletter in his name describes HB 2438 on online voter registration websites, reported out favorably by the House and sent to a Senate committee.
